newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Major arrives at palace to meet Queen.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Major arrives at palace to meet Queen.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major arrived at Buckingham Palace at around 1130 GMT on Monday for an audience with head of state Queen Elizabeth.
The Conservative prime minister was expected to ask the Queen to dissolve parliament, paving the way for an election on May 1.

As head of state, the queen must give her formal approval for parliament to be dissolved and an election called. Officials said Major was expected to make a statement on the steps of his Downing Street official residence at around 1230 GMT.
A Downing Street official said the prime minister was in good spirits. "He was extremely upbeat, very fresh, very alert, keen to get on to the business of the day and in fighting form," he said.
The opposition Labour party is around 20 points ahead of the Conservatives in opinion polls.

Labour, which has moved away from its socialist roots to the centre ground of British politics under Blair, needs a 4.3 percent swing to win power for the first time since 1979, larger than any it has achieved since 1945.
